newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse sets measures against trading halts.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse sets measures against trading halts.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange Inc said on Tuesday its board had approved measures to ensure that the session continued even when one of the trading floors was hit by a power failure or computer fault.

"If for any reason one trading floor cannot operate, the chairman or the president can authorise trading to start on the other trading floor at 10 a.m. local time (0200 GMT)," chief operating officer Rafael Llave said in a statement.
On Monday, the Philippine Stock Exchange had to cancel trading after a power failure hit its Ortigas trading floor.
The exchange said trading will resume at both the Tektite floor in Ortigas and at the Makati trading floor at 9:30 a.m. (0130 GMT) on Tuesday.
The two floors are electronically linked to prevent arbitrage opportunities and whenever one of the rings has been affected, the bourse has completely halted trading.

"Under a one trading floor only scenario, affected brokers may trade on the other trading floor through their correspondent brokers. Trades done this way shall be on a no commission basis. Affected brokers may send their traders to go to the booths of their correspondent brokers to assist. The correspondent brokers shall allow at least one of these traders inside their trading booths," the exchange statement said.
The exchange said that whenever the start of trading was delayed, it would close the market at 12:30 p.m. (0430 GMT).
Trading normally ends at noon (0400 GMT).
The exchange said it has to seek approval of the Securities and Exchange Commission on the extension of trading hours.
